Goldie Sayers placed 11th in the Javelin, not so far behind her season's best, but Scot Thompson was out of sorts as he was only able to manage 48.89 in the discus, some 7 metres down on his best for the year.

In the World Student Games, we were represented by Chris Lambert (won gold in the 100 m), Matt Douglas (won silver in the 400m hurdles and bronze in the 4x400 m relay), Goldie Sayers and Michelle Carey.

Maureen Knight placed second in the javelin where she deputised for Goldie Sayers, on Under-23 international duty in Poland Chris Moss back on the track after his knee injury was always in control of the 800 metres.

Ben Challenger is Britain’s sole high jumper and Goldie Sayers is our women’s javelin representative. Phillips Idowu was originally named to take part in the triple jump - subject to fitness - but has now withdrawn.
A third successive javelin title went to Goldie Sayers who although a little down on distance in this competition has thrown a lifetime best of 61.45 metres this summer.

Javelin thrower Goldie Sayers placed twelfth in the World Championships and fourth in the World Student Games; while Birhan Dagne, our national cross-country champion from 2004 continues to shine in road races all over the country.

Goldie Sayers had to be satisfied with 5th in the Javelin competition, unable to get her timing right. She occupied third place after two rounds, with 55.79 and improved her distance to 57.29 with a last effort but on this occasion a 60 metre throw was beyond her and the medals were just out of reach.
